projects.title: Minimal primitives: loops, schedules, goals, message passing — and the one missing wait
projects.objective: Owner direction 2026-08-21, REVERSING the previous plan in this project: do NOT add a review-shaped termination variant. Review is a category/description, open-ended, and must sit on top of minimal primitives rather than becoming a type. The primitive set is loops, schedules (cron/interval), goals (termination conditions), and message passing; everything specific composes from those. The repo already has this rule and it was being violated: CLAUDE.md hard rules say provider-bespoke values pass through verbatim as z.string() with no shared enums — yet 6 of the 14 buddy operations (delegate, request_review, complete_assignment, submit_review, complete_delegation, request_human_approval) are one shape, "send to a party and get a reply later", split into a hardcoded delegation/review/approval trichotomy. GROUND TRUTH: delegate ALREADY creates a fresh conversation for a real Buddy with its own soul and memory (routes.ts:419-444), which is exactly the "reviewer with personality and memory and fresh context" the Owner wants. The single missing primitive is the WAIT — routes.ts:449 returns 201 as soon as the child conversation is bound, never when it completes. Nothing in the system blocks.
projects.definition_of_done: A Buddy can run a goal loop that dispatches work to another Buddy with fresh context plus soul and memory, and waits for the reply, without any review-specific type existing anywhere. "Review" appears only as prose in a goal and as an open-ended purpose string, never as a variant in a sum or an enum. Achieved either by loop-as-wait (no new code) or by a generic blocking send, with deadlock and timeout behaviour specified.
projects.next_action: Owner decides Option A (loop-as-wait, free) vs Option B (blocking send). Design doc written 2026-08-21; nothing is implemented.

todos.title: Confirm with the Owner that goal-scoped workers are ordinary Buddies running a loop automation, NOT a third lifetime between ephemeral and direct report

OPTION A (free, today): the loop IS the wait. Request review in iteration N, poll get_inbox for the outcome in N+1, incorporate, continue. Zero new primitives — pure prose in termination.condition. Blocked only by the 10-iteration cap.

OPTION B (new primitive): a generic blocking send that returns the reply. Feasible despite -p because MCP tool calls are request/response — the parent stays alive blocked INSIDE a tool call, not on a pending turn. The scheduler already proves the server can await a conversation turn (runBeforeDeadline).

If Option B: deadlock is the real risk (A waits B waits A). Needs cycle/depth rejection in the write path, not a caller assertion — precedent exists, the store already cycle-walks relationships inside a #tx at store.js:1506.
If Option B: a blocking call must have a deadline, and for automation-driven callers the blocked child time counts against the parent's max_runtime_seconds. Specify both.

Consolidation candidate: collapse the 6 send/reply operations toward a generic send with an open-ended kind/purpose string. Large refactor — decide whether it precedes or follows the wait primitive; do NOT bundle silently.
